newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public TV group seeks extra cash - papers.
newsitem.headline: French public TV group seeks extra cash - papers.

text.p: France Television, which groups the two general French public television stations, has asked the government for 150 million francs extra next year, newspapers said on Friday.

They said Xavier Gouyou-Beauchamps, chairman of France Television, was seeking an extra 65 million francs ($10.7 million) for France 2, the bigger popular station of the two, and 85 million francs more for France 3 for 1998.

"He argued notably that extra expenses caused by coverage of the election campaign, an unforseeable event at the time when the Assembly (Parliament) voted the (1997) budget, had added some 20 million francs to the costs of each channel," financial daily Les Echos said.
A France Television spokesman declined comment on the reports.

Earlier this month France 2 posted a net loss of 199.3 million francs for 1996, compared with a 1995 profit of 60.7 million francs. Its 1996 budget was 4.88 billion francs of which the government funded 2.35 billion.
Les Echos said the channel could end 1997 around breakeven. France 3 showed a net profit of nine million francs in 1996, daily paper Liberation said.

A source close to France Television said the public television group was seeking permission to spend an extra 150 million francs next year, but if advertising receipts grew enough to cover the gap, it would take no extra public cash.
"All that depends on the advertising market and the effect of big groups' advertising spending," said the source, who declined to be identified.

Advertising receipts fund around half the budget at France 2 and France 3, while France's specialist public channels, cultural channels Arte and La Sept and educational channel La Cinquieme, carry no advertising and are funded entirely from the public purse.

At France 2 advertising receipts were up in the first half of this year, but at France 3 the picture was less strong in the first half, the source said. -- Paris newsroom +331 4221 5452 ($ = 6.056 French Francs)
